I believe the recent reddit modtalk leaks makes this argument succinctly enough, but I'm going to expand on this anyway.

I'm the main mod for a non-reddit community that gets a few million hits a month. I am extremely careful to not make many behind-the-scenes actions. Sunlight is the best disinfectant sort of stuff. How to implement this is tricky, but I'm of the belief that the duties of moderation will not be taken lightly. Anything you do - and I mean anything - will eventually be found out.

Totally agree a lot more transparency in moderation could be implemented. Tossing around a few ideas in my head, so I'll just lay them down here for now:

Each subverse sidebar should have a line reserved for current moderation frequency over the past 3 months reduced to lowest common denominator (e.g. Posts 1/344 Comments 1/174) I honestly have no idea what a fair number is for an active board, but this useful information to readers of a sub. Users can make their own decision on what's acceptable for the sub activity and subject matter. Furthermore this could go right under the current mod list and be clickable to more detailed information.

Deletions should only be reserved for EXTREME violations of rules. Illegal content, Doxxing, and I can't think of much else other than a user deleting their own posts. Mods need softer tools to keep conversations civil and on topic. They should have the power to hide a comment or post preventing any more voating as well as leave a reason so other readers can understand why this content is off topic and unwelcome in the sub. Separate from hiding they should also have the ability to lock posts and threads to further moderate unwelcome sub content. Hiding and locking should be independent from each other. There are many reasons why you may want to hide and not lock, or vice versa, or both.

While I'll admit I've never volunteered as a sub mod, I have been employed as community mod. Locking content, and leaving a response why, as well as perhaps including a link to duplicate or similar content goes a long way to organizing users to the original/official post and not come off as a deleting bag of dicks.
